author: Miramel86
title: Bait and Switch
content:
TLDR: Not like the ads, at all.

I saw an interactive ad for this game which featured a sushi chef churning out sushi on a conveyor belt for customers, and you selected which ingredient to use next to fulfill orders. Something about it tickled my smooth brain so I figured I’d download it.

I was suspicious that none of the pictures looked like the ad I played, but I thought perhaps there’s multiple game modes. I got started, glumly slogging through tutorials of the simple match mechanics, hoping to unlock this mysterious sushi mode. 30 minutes…60 minutes…90 minutes…nary a sushi in sight, just the same mindlessly repetitive matching and uninspired unlocks for “new” items that did nothing but clog up this tiny checkerboard that apparently makes up the core game mechanic.

At the 2 hour mark I admitted defeat. Perhaps this Sushi mode exists (apparently the internet tells me it’s a limited time event or some such) but I don’t care to waste more of my time. I found a hot pot game that scratches a similar itch and deleted this mess from my phone.

title: “Fun at First, but Becomes Nearly Impossible”
content:
I really enjoy Tasty Travels, but the game becomes extremely frustrating once you reach the higher levels. At a certain point, completing the weekly tasks feels almost impossible.

I spend hours throughout the day merging and trying to complete orders, and I’ve even purchased diamonds to help me progress. Despite spending both time and money on the game, I still find myself unable to complete the weekly goals. It feels like the difficulty increases to the point where progress is intentionally slowed down unless you keep spending more and more money.

I understand that a game needs to be challenging, and I don’t expect everything to be easy. But there is a difference between challenging and nearly impossible. If a player is actively playing throughout the day AND purchasing diamonds, they should at least have a realistic chance of completing the weekly tasks.

I really hope the developers reconsider the difficulty and balance at higher levels. I actually like the game and would like to keep playing, but lately it feels more frustrating than fun.

author: Anon.43
title: Must Spend Money to actually play. Waste of time.
content:
I don’t know how the reviews are saying that this game has steady game progression without spending any money. Completely false. At the BEGINNING of the game, there is steady game progression to get you hooked. You can level up about 15 levels relatively fast and upgrade structures and build new ones quickly. You can unlock new items and expand the board fast. 

But after that, once they start introducing challenges, it’s practically impossible to level up in a timely manner without either (1) spending money (repeatedly! Not one and done) or (2) spending an unreasonable amount of time playing the game/ waiting 3+ hours. I’ve been on the same level for about a week and this is with me playing the game every day for at least an hour or two. This is with me strategizing my energy and prioritizing orders with bigger rewards. This is with me trying to plan ahead and spend coins and energy and gems wisely. 

I used to enjoy this game the first week I played it, but after that, I realized that they simply do not give you enough energy to make any reasonable progress during a game session, do not give you enough ways to earn energy without spending money, do not give you enough of a payout for items you make that you don’t need yet it takes way more gems to pop the bubble of an item you do need with no way without spending money to earn said gems (for example: I don’t need item A, sells for 4 coins yet it took over 80 energy points to make??? I need item B but to pop this bubble it’ll take 36 gems??? we barely receive gems, you could basically never get these items), they do not give you enough gems, they do not give you enough coins for completing orders, it’s just ridiculous. The amount of energy and effort you will put into making an item you will not receive back. So what takes multiple sessions of gameplay to complete will not even get you to the next level.

Plus the amount of pop-ups you get to try and entice you to buy is frankly intrusive and unreasonable. Basically, every time you need more energy, 2 to 3 ads to buy energy pops up. EVERY. SINGLE. TIME. There’s just simply way too many things wrong with this game. It doesn’t make for fun gameplay unless you’re spending money.
